images.filename: Cotton Exchange Building, Union Avenue and Front Street, Memphis, TN (53699320910).jpg
images.caption: Built in 1922-1925, this Renaissance Revival-style skyscraper was designed by Mahan and Broadwell with C. G. Rosenplanter to house the Memphis Cotton Exchange, part of the cotton trading sector of the Memphis economy.  The building features a buff brick exterior, terra cotta trim, terra cotta spandrel panels on the principal facades, metal-frame windows, a terra cotta-clad base, arched transoms at the first floor bays, suspended canopies over the main entrance bays, decorative tapered doric pilasters, brick pilasters flanking the window bays on the principal facades with corinthian terra cotta capitals, and decorative reliefs.  Inside, the building features an intact lobby with a terrazzo floor, a ceiling with a decorative cornice, brass elevator doors with dial indicators flanked by reliefs of carved animal heads, marble-clad walls, and brass chandeliers.  The building is a contributing structure in the Cotton Row Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1979.  Today, the building houses various commercial office tenants, as well as the Cotton Museum of Memphis.

images.filename: Stax Museum of American Soul Music marquee.jpg
images.caption:
Stax Museum of American Soul Music — exterior marquee. 

A fabulous stop for any music lover. In the heart of Soulsville USA and located at the site of the original Stax Recording Studios.
The museum pays tribute to Stax legendary artist roster including unknowns who would become icons, cranking out a massive catalog of smash soul hits by the likes of Isaac Hayes, Otis Redding, the Staple Singers, Wilson Pickett, Luther Ingram, Albert King, the Bar-Kays, Booker T. & the MG's, Johnnie Taylor, Rufus and Carla Thomas, and dozens of other non-Stax artists who contributed to the soul music landscape.
The Otis Redding tribute is incredible.
